ColonyCouncil.RoomTemplateDef.label: roomy bedroom
ColonyCouncil.RoomTemplateDef.description: A large bedroom for one: bed, bedside table, dresser, an armchair, a light and plants. Space alone makes it impressive.
ColonyCouncil.RoomTemplateDef.purpose: For colonists who have earned more than a bed and a lamp, and for anyone the colony wants to keep happy.

tips.li: A 6x6 room is "spacious" even with a bed, a dresser and an armchair in it. Space counts toward impressiveness.
Greedy and jealous colonists care most about their bedroom. Give them the big one.
A dresser and a bedside table next to the bed make sleep a little more restful.

ColonyCouncil.RoomTemplateDef.label: sleeping hut
ColonyCouncil.RoomTemplateDef.description: A small sleeping room in the tribal way: a bedroll, a torch and a straw floor. Quick to raise from wood.
ColonyCouncil.RoomTemplateDef.purpose: A room of one's own before the colony has much of anything.

tips.li: A private hut beats a shared tent. Even a small room spares a colonist the barracks penalty.
Keep torches a few cells from the bed in wooden huts, and keep the door shut in winter.
A campfire nearby, not inside, warms a cluster of huts without filling them with smoke.

ColonyCouncil.RoomTemplateDef.label: roomy couple's bedroom
ColonyCouncil.RoomTemplateDef.description: A large bedroom for two: a double bed with a table on each side, a dresser, an armchair, a light and plants.
ColonyCouncil.RoomTemplateDef.purpose: For a couple the colony wants to keep: spouses, or two colonists whose moods hold others up.

tips.li: Both partners get the bedroom's mood every morning, so a fine shared room counts twice.
A bedside table on each side means neither partner misses out.

ColonyCouncil.RoomTemplateDef.label: small barracks
ColonyCouncil.RoomTemplateDef.description: Shared sleeping quarters for four, with a light. A first shelter that doesn't take long to build.
ColonyCouncil.RoomTemplateDef.purpose: A roof and a bed for the first few colonists, until there's time for bedrooms.

tips.li: Four to a room is easier on sleep than eight: fewer people get up in the night.
Plan the bedrooms as soon as the food is safe. The shared-bedroom penalty grows as the colony gets richer.

ColonyCouncil.RoomTemplateDef.label: small dining room
ColonyCouncil.RoomTemplateDef.description: A table for four with chairs, a light and a plant. Enough for a young colony.
ColonyCouncil.RoomTemplateDef.purpose: Somewhere to eat that isn't the floor. Every meal at a table spares the "ate without table" penalty.

tips.li: Four chairs feed about eight colonists if meals are spread over the day.
Put it next to the kitchen; a dining room is easy to extend later with a bigger plan.

ColonyCouncil.RoomTemplateDef.label: large dining room
ColonyCouncil.RoomTemplateDef.description: A long table for twelve with chairs all around, two lights and plants in the corners.
ColonyCouncil.RoomTemplateDef.purpose: Twelve seats: a big colony eats at once, and the hall it eats in counts for every meal.

tips.li: The dining room is the room colonists see most often. Decorate this one before the others.
A big impressive dining room is also a good place for parties, weddings and the council's meetings.
Keep a door to the kitchen and another to the corridors, so cooks and diners don't queue at one.

ColonyCouncil.RoomTemplateDef.label: large kitchen
ColonyCouncil.RoomTemplateDef.description: Two cooking stations, two shelves for ingredients, a light and a clean floor.
ColonyCouncil.RoomTemplateDef.purpose: Two cooks at once, for a colony that eats more than one stove can keep up with.

tips.li: Two stoves let one cook keep simple meals coming while the other works on fine meals or packaged survival meals.
Keep raw food on the shelves here and the rest in the freezer next door. Fewer steps, fresher food.

ColonyCouncil.RoomTemplateDef.label: large freezer
ColonyCouncil.RoomTemplateDef.description: A big cold store: three coolers built into the back wall and shelves in rows.
ColonyCouncil.RoomTemplateDef.purpose: Enough cold space for a season's harvest and the meat of a whole herd.

tips.li: [!lowtech] Three coolers hold a big room below freezing through most summers. Add a fourth in a heat wave.
[!lowtech] The coolers' hot side faces out of the back wall. Leave that side open, or vent it outdoors.
Rows of shelves with a walkway between them let haulers reach every shelf without walking around.

ColonyCouncil.RoomTemplateDef.label: large storeroom
ColonyCouncil.RoomTemplateDef.description: A big roofed room lined with shelves, with a walkway down the middle.
ColonyCouncil.RoomTemplateDef.purpose: One place for the colony's materials, out of the rain and close to the workshops.

tips.li: Shelves stack three items to a cell. A full storeroom of shelves holds far more than the same floor.
Set the shelves near the workshop to the materials the benches use most.

ColonyCouncil.RoomTemplateDef.label: small workshop
ColonyCouncil.RoomTemplateDef.description: One crafting station, a shelf for its materials and a light. A start before a real workshop.
ColonyCouncil.RoomTemplateDef.purpose: A bench with a roof over it, so the crafter's work isn't rained on and the bench stays clean.

tips.li: A workbench outdoors slows work and gets dirty. Even a small room with a floor helps.
Swap the bench for whatever the colony needs most: tailoring before winter, a smithy before raids.

ColonyCouncil.RoomTemplateDef.label: large workshop
ColonyCouncil.RoomTemplateDef.description: Four workstations around a free floor, a tool cabinet between the two at the back, and good light.
ColonyCouncil.RoomTemplateDef.purpose: All the colony's making in one room: clothes, weapons, parts and art, close to one storeroom.

tips.li: A tool cabinet speeds up work at benches near it. One between two benches serves both.
Workshops get messy. A cleaning colonist or a sterile floor keeps work quality up.
Put the storeroom door right next to this one: crafters walk to the materials for every bill.

ColonyCouncil.RoomTemplateDef.label: large laboratory
ColonyCouncil.RoomTemplateDef.description: A wide research bench, a multi-analyzer beside it, a bookcase and good light on a clean floor.
ColonyCouncil.RoomTemplateDef.purpose: The laboratory for the long research ahead: the hi-tech bench and its analyzer in one quiet room.

tips.li: A multi-analyzer near a hi-tech research bench speeds up research there. It needs the Multi-analyzer research first.
Books on a bookcase in the room add a research bonus nearby.
Keep the laboratory away from the dining and rec rooms, where people walk through and talk.

ColonyCouncil.RoomTemplateDef.label: infirmary
ColonyCouncil.RoomTemplateDef.description: Two beds with a vitals monitor between them, a medicine shelf, a light and a clean floor.
ColonyCouncil.RoomTemplateDef.purpose: A small, clean room for the sick and the wounded, so the wounded are never treated on the floor.

tips.li: Two beds cover most raids for a small colony. Set them to "medical" once they're built.
A vitals monitor helps the beds next to it. Between two beds, it helps both.

ColonyCouncil.RoomTemplateDef.label: hospital ward
ColonyCouncil.RoomTemplateDef.description: Nine beds, four vitals monitors, a medicine shelf, two lights and a clean floor.
ColonyCouncil.RoomTemplateDef.purpose: For a big colony, or one that fights often: a bed for every patient after a bad raid or an outbreak.

tips.li: A plague or a mass-casualty raid fills beds fast. A ward keeps the patients off the floor.
Keep a clean floor and a cleaner on it. Infections kill more colonists than the wounds do.
Build it near the main entrance and the battle line, so rescuers carry the wounded a short way.
